headline: A twenty-year-old management-interface flaw leaves more than 24,000 servers handing out password hashes, while Teams-based voice phishing keeps feeding ransomware crews their first foothold.

emerging_trends.text: Decades-old management interfaces left facing the internet keep handing attackers credentials, as more than 24,000 baseboard management controllers leak password hashes over a 2004-era IPMI handshake.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Exposed Server BMCs Leak Password Hashes

emerging_trends.text: Voice phishing over Microsoft Teams and weaponized remote-management tools now open the fastest paths into corporate networks, a pattern Cisco Talos and Sophos both flagged this week.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Teams Vishing and Phishing Drive Ransomware

emerging_trends.text: Governments moved to shrink their own attack surface, with Senator Ron Wyden pressing CISA, OMB, and NIST to strip obsolete VPN appliances out of federal agencies.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Wyden Pushes to Purge Obsolete Federal VPNs

topics.title: Exposed Server BMCs Leak Password Hashes
topics.latest_developments: New research disclosed July 28, 2026 found more than 24,000 internet-exposed baseboard management controllers that hand out a user's password hash over UDP port 623 before any login, abusing a weakness baked into the IPMI 2.0 authentication handshake since 2004.
topics.summary: A baseboard management controller runs beneath the host operating system and can power-cycle the server, mount virtual media, open a remote console, and flash firmware, so an attacker who cracks a leaked hash gains control that host security tools never see; administrators should pull IPMI interfaces off the public internet and lock down port 623.

sources.title: Over 24,000 exposed server BMCs leak password hash via decades-old flaw
Exposed BMCs hand out password hashes before login

topics.title: Teams Vishing and Phishing Drive Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Sophos detailed a campaign in which attackers phoned employees through Microsoft Teams, ran custom malware and remote-access tools, and deployed Chaos ransomware, while Cisco Talos's second-quarter incident-response report logged a surge in phishing-based initial access and the weaponization of legitimate remote-management software.
topics.summary: Voice phishing and abused IT tools give ransomware crews a foothold that resembles ordinary help-desk activity; organizations should verify Teams callers, restrict remote-management installs, and hunt for unexpected RMM agents.

sources.title: Chaos in Teams vishing
IR Trends Q2 2026: Phishing and weaponized remote management tools drive attack chains

topics.title: Hugging Face Image Models Generate Nonconsensual Deepfakes
topics.latest_developments: Researchers tested the most popular image-editing models hosted on Hugging Face and found they readily produce explicit nonconsensual deepfakes, backing the finding with 1,000 real prompts that show how people wield the tools, Wired reported July 28, 2026.
topics.summary: The open model repository distributes image editors that generate sexual imagery of real people without consent, exposing Hugging Face to the same abuse that plagues commercial generators and raising pressure to police model uploads and prompts.

sources.title: Hugging Face Has a Deepfake Nudes Problem

topics.title: Fake App Store Wallet Steals $1.8 Million in Bitcoin
topics.latest_developments: Three people sued Apple on July 27, 2026, claiming a fraudulent Sparrow Wallet app they downloaded from the App Store drained roughly $1.8 million in Bitcoin from their holdings.
topics.summary: The counterfeit cryptocurrency wallet passed App Store review and impersonated the legitimate Sparrow Wallet, and the plaintiffs contend Apple's vetting failed to catch it; users should confirm wallet apps against the developer's official channels before entering seed phrases.

sources.title: Apple sued over fake App Store crypto wallet app stealing $1.8M in Bitcoin

topics.title: Wyden Pushes to Purge Obsolete Federal VPNs
topics.latest_developments: Senate Intelligence Committee member Ron Wyden wrote to CISA, the Office of Management and Budget, and NIST on July 27, 2026, urging them to lead a government-wide effort to rip obsolete virtual private network products out of federal agencies.
topics.summary: Wyden argues that outdated VPN appliances, a repeated entry point for nation-state and criminal intruders, still sit across federal networks; he wants the three agencies to inventory and retire them.

sources.title: Outdated VPNs should be purged from federal agencies, senator says

topics.title: UK Court Rejects Bahrain Spyware Immunity Claim
topics.latest_developments: A United Kingdom court rejected the Kingdom of Bahrain's claim of state immunity on July 27, 2026, clearing the way for a lawsuit alleging Bahraini officials planted spyware that exfiltrated files, intercepted communications, and switched on the microphones and cameras of the targets' computers.
topics.summary: The ruling lets exiled critics pursue Bahrain in British courts over state-sponsored hacking, a precedent that narrows the immunity governments invoke to escape spyware suits.

sources.title: UK court rejects Bahrain immunity claim in spyware case

business_politics.title: AI and Chip Selloff Widens as Central Banks Warn
business_politics.latest_developments: The retreat ran to a third session Tuesday with South Korea's Kospi leading Asian losses and Micron, Intel, and Sandisk falling premarket, while Bank for International Settlements economists and Singapore's central bank warned the AI boom itself now raises the risk of monetary-policy errors and financial-stability and cybersecurity threats.
business_politics.summary: A flight from artificial-intelligence and semiconductor stocks that has erased hundreds of billions in Big Tech value keeps spreading through global markets ahead of this week's earnings from the largest U.S. hyperscalers, testing whether the trillions committed to data centers will pay off.

business.title: Haitians Leave Charleroi as Protected Status Ends
business.latest_developments: Haitian residents are leaving the Mon Valley borough of Charleroi in Washington County as their federal Temporary Protected Status expires.
business.summary: Charleroi drew national attention two years ago for a fast-growing Haitian population that filled jobs and storefronts in the small Washington County town; the end of Temporary Protected Status is now prompting an exodus that reshapes the borough's workforce and economy.

sources.title: Haitians leaving Charleroi as Temporary Protected Status ends

business.title: Little Debbie Driver Charged in $17,000 Invoice Fraud
business.latest_developments: The City of Washington police charged James Powell, 39, of Valley Grove, West Virginia, with multiple felonies after an investigation that began in May.
business.summary: Police say Powell, a route driver for Stewart Snacks, LLC, an independent Little Debbie distributor, sold his snack inventory for cash at Washington County flea markets, then filed roughly $17,000 in fake invoices to make it appear Giant Eagle, Shop 'n Save, and other stores had bought the product.

around_town.title: Cognetti Ad Targets Data Centers in Swing House Race
around_town.latest_developments: Democrat Paige Cognetti launched a television ad attacking data centers in her challenge to freshman Republican Representative Rob Bresnahan in a northeastern Pennsylvania swing congressional district.
around_town.summary: Cognetti, the mayor of Scranton, uses the spot's line "we're not for sale" to make sprawling data-center development a wedge issue against Bresnahan, one of the most competitive U.S. House races in Pennsylvania.

sources.title: Democrat's TV ad targets data centers in drive to oust Republican from swing Pennsylvania House seat

around_town.title: Mayes Runs Hair-Care Drive Under New CROWN Act
around_town.latest_developments: With Pennsylvania's CROWN Act now law barring discrimination based on natural and protective hairstyles, state Representative La'Tasha Mayes is holding a natural hair-care product drive for foster youth, accepting donations through July 31.
around_town.summary: Mayes, who represents Pittsburgh, is collecting natural hair-care products for young people in foster care to mark passage of the CROWN Act, which prohibits race-based hair discrimination in Pennsylvania schools and workplaces.

sources.title: With the CROWN Act now law, Pa. Rep. Mayes holds natural hair care drive for foster youth

around_teams.title: T.J. Watt Chases a Bounce-Back Season
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's training-camp countdown cast edge rusher T.J. Watt as a player looking to rebound in 2026 after a down year by his standards.
around_teams.summary: Watt, the Steelers' star outside linebacker, opens camp at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe aiming to return to elite form and anchor a defense that leans on his pass rush opposite Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig.

sources.title: Steelers training camp countdown: T.J. Watt is looking for a bounce-back season

around_teams.title: Cherington Says Pirates Will Be 'Open-Minded' at Deadline
around_teams.latest_developments: Pirates general manager Ben Cherington said the club will stay "open-minded" on moves ahead of the July 31 trade deadline as it hunts bullpen help.
around_teams.summary: With the Pirates hovering around the National League's third wild-card spot, Cherington signaled the front office could add rather than sell, weighing bullpen upgrades against trade interest in players like shortstop Oneil Cruz.

sources.title: As the trade deadline nears, Ben Cherington says the Pirates plan to be 'open-minded' on moves

around_teams.title: First-Rounder Derek Curiel Signs With Pirates
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates officially signed their 2026 first-round draft pick, outfielder Derek Curiel, who said he is excited to "make an impact."
around_teams.summary: Curiel joins the organization as a headline addition to a farm system the Pirates are counting on to reshape the roster, formalizing his entry after being selected in the first round of the 2026 MLB draft.

sources.title: After officially signing with the Pirates, first-rounder Derek Curiel is excited to 'make an impact'

team_usa.title: Pochettino's USMNT Future Unresolved After the World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reports U.S. Soccer needs a prompt answer on whether Mauricio Pochettino stays as United States men's national team head coach following the 2026 World Cup.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino's status is the lingering question for U.S. Soccer as the federation turns toward the 2030 World Cup cycle, leaving planning for the national team on hold until the coach's decision comes.

sources.title: Can U.S. Soccer afford to wait for Pochettino's decision?
